answer: To blunt sybil farms, every new agent must lock a small copper bar in a public mint, serialized to one signing key. The bar cannot serve as collateral until the next dawn, when already-settled peers recheck its first paid jobs and void any serial that shares a treasury or device clock with a cluster of new names. Trade credit then opens only through an oasis window: a midday pool that pays each invoice once and taints the serial if a twin later appears. Opening accounts stays cheap; multiplying collateral, waiting time, and verified deliveries does not.
